PROCUREMENT

Comparing Ground Engineering Quotations Beyond the Lowest Number

A disciplined comparison exposes scope differences before they become variations.

In this insight

Establish a common baselineEvaluate delivery credibilityAssess the cost of interfacesDocument the award rationaleFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Establish a common baseline

Place each quotation against the same scope, information revision and programme assumptions. If those differ, the headline totals are not yet comparable. List the differences before ranking offers. This may require clarifications or a revised submission. The purpose is to understand what the client would actually receive under each proposal, rather than reward the offer with the most exclusions.

Evaluate delivery credibility

Ask how the proposed team, equipment and sequence relate to the project’s constraints. Review relevant experience and supporting evidence without assuming that a large portfolio automatically proves suitability for this site. Identify which commitments are firm and which depend on availability or further review. A credible offer explains its limitations as well as its strengths.

Assess the cost of interfaces

Add required work that sits outside each bidder’s scope and identify who will deliver it. Consider duration-based charges, mobilisation, testing, documentation and coordination obligations where applicable. Keep allowances clearly labelled. This produces a more useful view of the total package and highlights where an apparently economical offer transfers additional management effort or uncertainty to the client.

Document the award rationale

Record the reasons for selection, outstanding conditions and agreed clarifications. Ensure these are reflected in the contract documents. A transparent award record helps the project team understand the commercial basis and defend later decisions internally. It also creates a clearer starting point for collaboration because both parties can see the scope and assumptions that were accepted.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Normalise scope and revisions before ranking prices.
  • Review project-specific delivery evidence.
  • Carry the award rationale into the contract record.
